claims.claim: Teradyne occupies a test bottleneck downstream of AI compute, HBM/DRAM and semiconductor production; Q2 2026 Semiconductor Test reached a second consecutive record quarter and memory revenue exceeded $200M for a third consecutive quarter.

Robotics provides a second automation pathway and reached $100M Q2 revenue with five consecutive quarters of sequential growth, but its end-market has shifted toward electronics manufacturing and semiconductor customers, increasing causal overlap rather than full diversification.
Test demand is structurally mediated by a limited set of significant customers and their supply partners, so aggregate AI capex does not translate one-for-one into Teradyne revenue.

falsifiers: AI/HBM production growth without Teradyne test growth would weaken bottleneck control.
Sustained robotics growth that remains unprofitable would weaken cross-division leverage.
Customer insourcing or competing test architectures materially reducing Teradyne share would weaken substitution resilience.

risks.risk: Semiconductor Test and Robotics increasingly share electronics/semiconductor end-market exposure.
Customer concentration can create nonlinear demand swings.

unknowns.unknown: This Beta object does not quantify current market share by AI compute or HBM test application.

claims.claim: Customer concentration is a present, disclosed risk: two Semiconductor Test customers represented about 22% and 20% of year-end 2025 accounts receivable.

Debt is real but not presently shown as covenant distress: Teradyne ended 2025 with $200M outstanding under its credit facility after repaying $50M, and was compliant with covenants as of February 19, 2026.
The strongest falsification pressure is cyclicality/concentration and execution in Robotics, not an unsupported claim of accounting weakness.

risks.risk: Two customers represented roughly 42% combined of year-end 2025 receivables.
Robotics execution remains a meaningful profitability/strategy risk despite improving revenue cadence.

unknowns.unknown: Latest proxy/SBC normalization and convertible-note derivative details remain Alpha underwriting inputs, not resolved by this Beta object.
